definition: Educational resources and programs designed to help users learn how to effectively use a software platform.
extendedDefinition: User training covers the resources and programs that teach people to use a software platform effectively, from guided walks and video courses to instructor-led sessions and certification tracks. Training determines adoption: a capable product under-taught returns far less than a modest product well-trained, because users fall back on habits and workarounds when they do not understand the tool. Buyers should assess training materials during evaluation, including their depth, role coverage, and availability in the organization's languages. Implementation plans should budget time for training ahead of rollout, since retroactive education is less effective and slower. For substantial deployments, administrator and trainer programs multiply impact, preparing internal champions to support their own teams. Measuring adoption after training, through feature usage and completion rates, closes the loop and identifies where additional support is needed. Vendors that invest in training reduce the buyer's implementation cost and accelerate time-to-value.
